authority_boundary: Graph edge types are a reviewed, closed, versioned vocabulary. Generated graph edges are candidate evidence unless a local review process promotes a downstream decision.

edge_types.semantics: A canonical lesson record names the repository where the lesson was learned.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Lessons can be routed to the wrong repo history.

edge_types.semantics: A lesson evidence pointer names a registered DAD offering.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Asset feedback and upgrade targeting can attach to the wrong offering.

edge_types.semantics: A lesson reusable-pattern value matches a reviewed pattern id or label.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Pattern-gap curation can be polluted by accidental prose matches.

edge_types.semantics: A repo usage ledger row says the repo is using an offering.
evidence_required: repo asset usage ledger row with status using
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Upgrade mail can target repos that are not using the asset.

edge_types.semantics: A repo usage ledger row says the repo is watching an offering for possible future use.
evidence_required: repo asset usage ledger row with status watching
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Future-use recommendations can spam repos with irrelevant upgrades.

edge_types.semantics: A declared lineage record says one mail packet, offering, or version replaces another.
evidence_required: declared supersedes field or lineage record
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Repos can retire or ignore the wrong asset version.

edge_types.semantics: A reviewed asset, skill, or offering names the intake or research record it was promoted from.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Research provenance can be lost or fabricated.

edge_types.semantics: A mail packet or lesson explicitly marks itself as a sighting of a reviewed pattern.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Pattern mining gets inflated by vague similarities.

edge_types.semantics: A reviewed offering or harness declares an eval case, test artifact, or validation command as supporting evidence.
evidence_required: declared validation artifact path or id

edge_types.semantics: A registry row explicitly declares an asset dependency.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Update ordering and affected-repo analysis can become wrong.

edge_types.direction: asset -> asset (symmetric pair stored once, lower id first)
edge_types.semantics: Two same-category assets are near-duplicate or variant candidates and must route through semantic-evolution review.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: DAD can collapse distinct assets or create duplicate systems.

edge_types.direction: asset -> asset (symmetric pair stored once, lower id first)
edge_types.semantics: Two assets cover adjacent, non-overlapping workflow stages for a shared task context.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: False complements pollute combination discovery and waste review time.

edge_types.direction: asset -> asset (symmetric pair stored once, lower id first)
edge_types.semantics: Usage traces show assets used together in one or more repo sessions.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: DAD can spam bundled recommendations based on accidental co-use.

edge_types.semantics: A failure, review finding, or lesson provides evidence for an unmet DAD need.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Research and build effort can be misdirected.

edge_types.semantics: An asset is a hypothesized member of a multi-asset workflow combination.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Workflow recommendations can bundle unrelated assets.
